findings.title: Judgment is made operative through restraint and repair
findings.claim: Within the declared 19:1-19:15 pericope, the focus piety is placed beside a practical pattern in which judgment checks force, protection inserts a barrier, and filial goodness gives repair a social form.
findings.mechanism: The 19:12 judgment occurrence meets the focus protective adjective, while 19:14 places filial goodness beside the same-root coercive form and departure from obedience. The supplied bridle, barrier, splint, and repair images therefore change judgment from an abstract verdict into disciplined force that preserves relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive why the focus's guarding quality belongs beside judgment and the next ayah's conduct: power becomes legible through what it restrains, protects, and repairs.
findings.containment: This keeps the ordinary judgment, piety, and filial readings intact. The bridle and splint images qualify the relation without making judgment identical with a physical object, and the channel does not claim that restraint exhausts judgment.

epistemic.reason: The channel is trusted and all eight nominated branches have exact supplied pericope carriers, while the synthesis remains a contextual macro image rather than a lexical replacement.

branch_activations.facet_statement: repairing fracture and lack
branch_activations.carrier: The 19:14 same-root coercion form supplies the surface carrier for the channel's repair image.

branch_activations.activation: The coercive carrier is contacted by judgment and protection, allowing the channel's repair branch to describe force redirected toward restoring integrity.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Judgment can be heard as a power that repairs a damaged relation rather than merely pronouncing on it.
branch_activations.boundary: The repair image remains contextual and does not turn جَبَّارًا into the ordinary lexical gloss of repair.

branch_activations.carrier: The 19:14 جَبَّارًا occurrence carries the supplied coercive-domination image.

branch_activations.activation: Coercive domination meets the protective and relational boundary in the surrounding portrait, so the focus's piety is read against force that overwhelms relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's guarded character is perceptible as a form of power that leaves room for relation rather than domination.
branch_activations.boundary: The activation preserves the contextual coercion contrast and does not make non-coercion the whole meaning of taqwa.

findings.title: Mercy is carried through generative care
findings.claim: Within the pericope, the focus tenderness, purity-growth, and piety can be heard as the formed continuation of a generative care process that moves from blocked generation through a ready gift, birth, early life, and filial conduct.
findings.mechanism: The mercy occurrence at 19:2 meets the repeated barrenness at 19:5 and 19:8, the gift at 19:5, the young child at 19:12, birth at 19:15, and the focus's tenderness, growth, and purity carriers. These contacts give the focus qualities a bodily and ethical formation sequence without changing their ordinary local senses.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the two gifts and the piety clause as a connected formation: care reaches the body, then continues as character and relation.
findings.containment: The womb and generative images remain contextual analogies. They do not reduce mercy to biology, make every later quality a literal womb sense, or replace the focus's ordinary servant-portrait context.

epistemic.reason: The trusted channel supplies the nominated branch images and exact pericope contacts; the unified bodily-and-ethical relation is still a qualified contextual synthesis.

branch_activations.activation: Filial care meets the focus gifts and child context, making the generative image continue into a relational way of living.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus tenderness is perceptible as care that reaches outward into maintained kinship.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch adds a contextual social consequence and does not replace the ordinary meaning of بَرًّا.

findings.title: A pastoral cycle mirrors managed dependence
findings.claim: Within the same pericope, the human birth scene can also be viewed through a pastoral cycle in which freshness, young dependence, blocked generation, birth, attachment, and eventual separation make continuity a managed relation.
findings.mechanism: The 19:2 freshness carrier, 19:5 and 19:8 barrenness, 19:11 early-time carrier, 19:13 focus yearning and tenderness, and 19:15 birth and repeated-time carriers contact the pastoral branches. Their sequence adds a material mirror of dependence and weaning to the focus portrait.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive continuity not only as a miracle or a finished result but as care held near the young until a later separation becomes possible.
findings.containment: This is a pastoral mirror of the human scene, not a claim that Yahya is an animal or that every pastoral facet is active. The ordinary human and ethical reading remains fully recoverable.

epistemic.reason: The trusted channel supplies exact nominated pastoral images and pericope contacts; the mirror relation is a bounded contextual synthesis rather than a lexical identification.

findings.title: The remembered mercy feeds a formed character
findings.claim: The focus tenderness and growth can be heard as the formed result of the mercy remembered at 19:2, with nurture giving that mercy a process of feeding, repair, and completion.
findings.mechanism: The exact 19:2 mercy and lordship occurrences contact the focus tenderness and growth occurrences. The attributed nurture and feeding roles make the focus qualities read as a developing outcome of the opening mercy rather than as unrelated gifts.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the focus tenderness as an active medium of formation, so the portrait holds both the source of care and the character it has produced.
findings.containment: The HFT source leaves open that the words may be parallel descriptions of one gift rather than a causal process. The nurture relation is attributed, and unresolved branches receive no lexical gloss or facet.

epistemic.reason: The trace is exact and internally complete, but its source is legacy_unbound and three branch records are unresolved; the process reading is therefore attributed.

findings.title: Piety appears as realized being
findings.claim: The focus clause can be heard as presenting piety not only as a predicate attached to Yahya but as a realized mode of being formed after the pericope has spoken of creation from prior nonbeing.
findings.mechanism: The 19:9 creation and negated-being carriers meet the focus growth noun and the affirmative كَانَ predicate. Their contrast gives the copular form an attributed ontic pressure: what was not a thing is now present in a stable moral state.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the final piety clause as an achieved presence within the created person, while still recovering the ordinary function of كَانَ as a predicate-bearing copula.
findings.containment: The HFT source leaves open that كَانَ remains ordinary predication with only rhetorical added force. The finding does not claim that the copula lexically means creation or that piety is mechanically produced by it.

epistemic.reason: The source coordinates and focus return are exact, but the source is legacy_unbound and the trace explicitly preserves an ordinary-predication alternative.

findings.title: Guarding takes a directed path
findings.claim: The added 1:6-1:7 contact can give the focus guarding quality a directional form: protection becomes movement along a guided straight path and away from straying.
findings.mechanism: The focus protection carrier and its core and wrong-conduct facets meet the external guidance, straight-path, bestowed-state, and straying occurrences. The path sequence adds destination and departure boundaries to the focus character beyond the native portrait.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive piety as a guard that helps conduct remain oriented, not merely as a private shield against danger.
findings.containment: This is a Phase 2 overlay and does not make taqwa mean path, import the whole Fatiha, or settle what the straight path means. The ordinary focus piety remains recoverable.

epistemic.reason: The focus protection facets and exact external path and outcome occurrences provide a specific local contact, but no dedicated support or connection record is supplied.
